title: Vanishing of a higher direct image, checked at a geometric point
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a
quasi-compact and
quasi-separated morphism of schemes, let $q\ge0$, and let $F$ be a
torsion etale sheaf on
$X_{\Et}$. Then $R^qf_*F=0$ if and only if for every geometric
point $\bar y$ of $Y$ the filtered colimit of the groups
$H^q(W\times_YX,F)$, taken over the
pointed etale
neighbourhoods $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar y$ (the strict local test
schemes of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]), vanishes.

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf] (Stacks Tag 03Q8), the sheaf $R^qf_*F$ is associated to the presheaf on $Y_{\Et}$ sending an etale $W\to Y$ to $H^q(W\times_YX,F|_{W\times_YX})$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-geometric-stalk], the sheafification map induces an isomorphism from the presheaf stalk to the stalk of its associated sheaf. The former is the colimit of the groups $H^q(W\times_YX,F|_{W\times_YX})$ indexed by the opposite of the category of pointed etale neighbourhoods $(W,\bar w)$ of $\bar y$, as in that lemma and [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Hence this colimit is canonically isomorphic to $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}$.

Put $G=R^qf_*F$ and apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to the unique morphism $0\to G$. The stalk of the zero sheaf is the zero group, since it is the colimit of zero groups. Thus the induced map on each geometric stalk is $0\to G_{\bar y}$; it is an isomorphism exactly when $G_{\bar y}=0$. The morphism $0\to G$ is an isomorphism exactly when $G$ is a zero object. Conservativity and the identification in step 2 therefore give both directions of the claimed equivalence.
